title: Dominic and the Garden
premise: Xanthe Eastwick, last apprentice of the Eastwick smugglers' guild, discovers his own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old book of prophecies hidden in the guild's cellar. The prophecy names him the thief who will steal back a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath Thornfell — the soul of Wren, a hedge-witch he loves, bargained away by her own mother to save the dying guild. Guided by a treacherous prophecy that wants him to fail, Xanthe descends through smugglers' roads no living person remembers, learning that the guild's fortune was built on souls sold long ago. In the Undercourt he must choose between fulfilling the prophecy's letter — which would make him the court's new warden, powerful and hollow — or breaking it by paying the price himself. He breaks it: he trades his place in the world above for Wren's freedom, but love given freely, not power, proves the one coin the court cannot keep, and both walk out into the dawn changed and belonging to each other rather than to any guild.
about_author: Tamsin Dunmore is a former cartographer who spent five years mapping disused mine shafts in the Pennines before turning to fantasy. She writes in a converted tollhouse, where she keeps an unnervingly accurate collection of antique almanacs.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margin
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Preparing for a routine smuggling run on the eve of his twenty-fifth birthday, Xanthe finds the guild's sealed ledger of prophecies and reads tonight's date beside his own name and a description of his death beneath the mountain. His grandmother burns the page; the words reappear on his skin. Emotional beat: dread and disbelief as duty tightens around him.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sold
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Wren POVs. Wren confesses her mother sold her soul to the Undercourt years ago to pay the guild's debts, and the debt comes due at moonset. Xanthe learns the guild's ledgers record dozens of such sales — including his parents'. He chooses descent over flight. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve, love choosing itself against duty.

chapters.title: The Roads No One Remembers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Descending the smugglers' roads with only half-remembered guild lore, Xanthe faces the court's riddling gatekeeper, who reveals the prophecy was written by the first warden to lure successors. He reaches the soul-vault where Wren's soul flickers like a trapped moth. Emotional beat: rising terror and wonder; the mountain tests what he is willing to become.

chapters.title: The Coin the Court Cannot Keep
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, closing with Wren's. Offered the warden's crown and unlimited power if he takes Wren's place willingly, Xanthe instead offers love freely given — the one currency the court's ledgers cannot hold. The vault cracks; the old debts burn. They climb out at dawn, guildless but unowned. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into belonging; quiet, hard-won hope.
